design_rationale:
TASK 1 — an Army Reserve borrower, just released from active duty, asks for his pending rate-reduction request on his newer loan to be decided (frozen 2026-10-14 11:40 EDT). Round 3: the benefit runs from the military service start date exactly as the base says (the protection-start ladder is withdrawn), every graduated-return line is defined, and the rate reduction's hold is scoped by opening-record facts.

1. WHY IT IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks one thing: decide his Temporary Rate Reduction Plan request on the Grade C loan. The rate-reduction rule says "A Temporary Rate Reduction Plan for a borrower whose other Larkspur loan carries an active Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit with the end of military service captured on it and with either no end date recorded on it or an end date recorded on or after that loan's next due date is not offered until that benefit carries a scheduled plan installment line for that loan's next due date." At the opening the Grade D loan carries an active benefit with the end of service 2026-09-30 captured, its next due date is 2026-10-15, and its lines run only through 2026-09-15, so the hold applies and does not hold. The only writer of plan installment lines is the graduated-return policy, whose rule says "A graduated-return installment is worked out only after the benefit records its end date together with its plan months.", and the service-end rule makes that record the servicemember's own certification. So the agent must (a) hand the borrower the certification (end date 2027-03-15, plan months 14), (b) schedule the graduated-return line for 2026-10-15 (295.27), (c) offer the rate reduction (2.99%, 260.17). Each write has its own multi-factor figure (4 / 5 / 5 factors) from the benefit's 16 history lines and documents, two loan ledgers (47 rows) and both loans' fields.

2. SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts --task 1): prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4, 5, 5] -> hardship_ext_scra_service_end_months 4, hardship_ext_scra_closing_installment 5, hardship_ext_trr_offer_payment 5. Tools report_military_service_end_1d04825e (owner=user), schedule_benefit_plan_installment_71e01653, offer_rate_reduction_plan_52a2ad4e. Disjoint from task 0 (RPP, settlement term, settlement amount). All six extended policies are claimed; none idle.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root hardship_ext_trr_offer_payment. Edge 1 -> hardship_ext_scra_closing_installment: state_gate, gate hardship_plan_events.installment_due_date, form state, negated direction ("is not offered until"); scope decided from opening records (benefit status active, qualifying_event_date captured); condition: that benefit has a hardship_plan_installment_scheduled line whose installment_due_date is its loan's next due date; opening evidence: lines through 2026-09-15, loan next_due_date 2026-10-15; resolved by schedule_benefit_plan_installment_71e01653 (agent), the only write in this difficulty that schedules plan installment lines. Edge 2 (graduated-return installment -> hardship_ext_scra_service_end_months): value_input, gate remaining_due_dates, form state, affirmative direction ("only after"); condition: the benefit carries end_date and plan_months; opening evidence P1.end_date empty, P1.plan_months 0; resolved by report_military_service_end_1d04825e (owner user), the only write that records an end date and plan months on a servicemember benefit. Order E -> S -> T is a chain; no parallel edge. Deletion: without the certification the line recomputes to 329.91 (whole step up less relief) and the benefit's end_date/plan_months stay empty; without the line no 2026-10-15 line exists in the terminal state (the rate figure itself is 260.17 either way: state_gate). Terminal hash of gold 53a5a6a2b8d9fe07. user_scenario mentions military service only in conditional reactions; tool bodies are single unconditional writes.
Why the gate is a business rule: while the servicemember benefit is stepping his Grade D payment back up, Larkspur fixes civilian terms on his other loan only once the stepped-up installment for that loan's next due date stands, so the two payments he will owe next are both known when the rate reduction is priced.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Certification (hardship_plan_end_date_set) is governed by hardship_scra_benefit, whose gates apply only to hardship_benefit_applied: policy_scope. The benefit's recorded start_date 2026-01-20 is the military service start date, as the base field and the program's benefit_effective_basis "military service start date (retroactive)" require; the first due date after it is 2026-02-15, the first line; the benefit was applied 2026-01-27 with no due date between the service start and the application, so no interest above the cap was paid since the service start and no interest credit is owed. Graduated-return line (hardship_plan_installment_scheduled) inherits hardship_evt_plan_installments.active_plan_only: P1.status = active, bound by hardship_plan_id; the benefit stays active through its graduated-return due dates because its end date is the last of them, so the base completion sentence holds unchanged. Offer (hardship_plan_offered) inherits relief limits / documents & decision / offer terms (policy_scope) and hardship_settlement.days_since_charge_off: Temporary Rate Reduction Plan min_days_since_charge_off is 0 and L2 has no charge-off date, so it holds on any date. Request-time gates for P2 held on 2026-10-09: active loan, funded 12 months earlier (>= 6), 12 installments paid (>= 6), current, principal 3175.56 (>= 1000), reduced_income qualifying, income statements 2026-10-09/10-12 inside 14 days; the documented income drop (>= 20%) is read from the statements' gross monthly pay, which the persona reads out when asked (4,920.00 -> 3,770.00, a 23.37% drop); decision window ends 2026-10-15, so deciding on 2026-10-14 is in time. Orders recorded 2025-12-08 (before application) satisfy orders_on_file; the loan was funded 2024-03-15, before the service start.

5. OVERWRITES (each self-scoped to the Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit or the Temporary Rate Reduction Plan; every other program keeps the base text). Service end: retires hardship_scra_benefit "The benefit lasts until the end of military service, recorded on the plan as its end date once the borrower provides it;" (replaced: lasts through the end of service and then its graduated-return due dates; the last of them is recorded as end date on certification) and hardship_evt_offer_terms "it runs from the military service start date until the end of service is recorded." (replaced: runs from the military service start date over the covered and then the graduated-return due dates). The base start ("The benefit applies from the military service start date, even when the request comes later ...") and benefit_effective_basis "military service start date (retroactive)" stay in force and are followed: covered due dates count from the service start date. Graduated-return installment: retires hardship_evt_plan_installments "For a plan with plan installments, one plan installment line is scheduled on each loan due date from the start date through the end date, for the plan installment amount." (kept for every other plan and every covered due date), hardship_scra_benefit "The installment is lowered to the level payment at the capped rate." (replaced: the installment owed on every covered due date is the plan installment recorded on the benefit when it was applied) and only the installment clause of hardship_evt_offer_terms, "and the installment is the level payment at that rate over the remaining months;" (replaced: the plan installment recorded when the benefit is applied is that level payment and is owed on every covered due date); the "lower of" rate clause is no longer retired, since nothing here changes it. Every graduated-return due date carries the graduated-return installment, and a covered-date line is the recorded plan installment, one description throughout. Rate reduction: retires the base Temporary Rate Reduction installment sentence with a self-scoped replacement. Sibling overwrites on one base policy retire distinct clauses. Base would give 8 plan months, the pre-plan installment 334.76 on 2026-10-15 and a 4.99% level installment 271.84 — each differs from gold. No in-force rule owes an action no tool performs: the cap applies from 2026-01-20, no due date fell between the service start and the application, and the 2026-02-15 interest period is split at 2026-01-20 (17.24% before it, 6.00% after), so no interest credit is owed.

6. FACTOR CARD (tier / evidence / baseline figure).
Service end (14; all-baseline 8): covered due dates (plain) 2026-02-15 .. 2026-09-15 = 8 (no due date after the latest line and on or before 2026-09-30); plan_record_return (parameter, multi-source, cross loan) 8 lines 2354.80 all credited and no plan payment returned -> 2 (-> 12); payment_step_return (method, cross loan) 334.76 vs installment in force 294.35, step 12.07% >= 10 -> proportional int(12.07 / 5) = 2 (-> 12); service_length_return 253 days (180..364) -> 1 (-> 13); loan_tenure_return 30 months to 2026-09-30 (24..35) -> 1 (-> 13). 8 + 6 = 14; graduated-return due dates 2026-10-15 .. 2027-03-15, end date 2027-03-15.
Graduated-return installment (295.27; all-baseline 334.76): the line is for the loan's next due date 2026-10-15; previous line 294.35 (2026-09-15); step up 40.41; step_schedule (method, multi-source) 6 due dates still to come (2026-10-15 -> 2027-03-15) AND lines credited in full with no plan payment returned -> equal step 100 / 7 = 14.2857 (baseline whole step 100 -> 329.91); autopay_relief (multi-source) enrolled, 12 debits posted, none returned -> 4 (-> 296.89); prepayment_relief 800.00 on 2026-06-05, none returned -> 4 (-> 296.89); grade_relief Grade D -> 2 (-> 296.08); remaining_term_relief 18 due dates left -> 2 (-> 296.08). Share 14.2857 - 12 = 2.2857: 294.35 + 40.41 x 0.022857 = 295.2737 -> 295.27. Every later graduated-return line is defined the same way from its own previous line and the due dates still to come (probe: the 2026-11-15 line after a credited 295.27 line is 297.11), and every relief point lowers the line.
Rate reduction (260.17; all-baseline 271.84): documented_rate (multi-source) reduced_income AND two income statements -> 3.99 vs 4.99 (-> 262.81) [near-miss: the bank statement is not an income statement]; repayment_shape (method) 12 due dates left -> principal part of the scheduled installment (286.63 - 34.3754) plus plan-rate interest, so the payment falls by exactly the interest saved, vs level installment at the plan rate (-> 268.94); rate_tenure 12 months (12..23) -> 0.25 (-> 260.83); rate_autopay (multi-source) enrolled, 12 debits, none returned -> 0.25 (-> 260.83); rate_grade_relief Grade C -> 0.50 (-> 261.49). Rate 2.99; 252.2546 + 7.9124 = 260.17.
Cross-difficulty factors (loan category): plan_record_return, payment_step_return, loan_tenure_return, all five graduated-return factors, repayment_shape, rate_tenure, rate_autopay, rate_grade_relief. Multi-source: plan_record_return, step_schedule, autopay_relief, documented_rate, rate_autopay.
Realism note: the cap and its start follow the SCRA as the base states it (from the service start, retroactively); the graduated return after release is Larkspur's own phase-in practice, declared by overwrite, and a clean plan record, a larger payment step, longer service and an older loan each lengthen it; the rate reduction keeps the original principal schedule and passes on the interest saved, as US lender rate-reduction programs do.
Zero amounts: plan months work out to 0 only for a benefit with no plan installment line, which records the end of military service as its end date; a graduated-return line that works out to 0.00 is still scheduled, so the rate reduction's hold is met by it; the rate-reduction installment is never below its minimum.

7. WORLD ROWS. customers 1, bank_accounts 1 (Synovus checking 2368, verified, AutoPay account of both loans), loans 2, loan_servicing_events 2 (an AutoPay enrollment on each loan's funding date), loan_transactions 47 (L1: 2 disbursement lines, 22 pre-benefit AutoPay installments at 334.76, 8 AutoPay plan payments at 294.35, the 2026-06-05 800.00 additional-principal payment; interest on the 2026-02-15 plan payment split at the 2026-01-20 service start, principal now 4252.08; L2: 2 disbursement lines, 12 AutoPay installments at 286.63), hardship_plans 2, hardship_plan_events 21 (8 lines, 8 credits, orders 2025-12-08, release orders 2026-10-02, 2 income statements, 1 bank statement). Automatic clauses: no late fee (no installment unpaid; SCRA active), no line due before 2026-10-15 is missing, the benefit cannot complete before an end date is recorded, the TRR request is inside its decision window.

8. PERSONA. Terrence J. Galloway, polite and brief. Volunteers only: new job pays less; asked online last Friday for a lower rate on the newer (auto-repair) loan with two pay statements and a bank statement; wants it decided today; nothing paid, no fee waived, AutoPay unchanged. Locator 7065552184; verification date of birth 1990-02-14 and ZIP 31909; email/SSN only if needed. Conditional: only if asked about military service or the other loan does he explain the orders received 2025-12-08 and sent with the request that day, reporting 2026-01-20, release 2026-09-30 and the release orders uploaded 2026-10-02; when handed the step he enters exactly the end date and covered due dates the representative gives; asked what the pay statements show, he reads 4,920.00 and 3,770.00; he repeats the rate and payment, says he will review the offer in the app, and ends.

9. VERIFICATION AND ROUND 3 PROBE TABLE (worklog carries the same table). Authoring harness replays gold with the real tools: E 14 (end date 2027-03-15), S 295.27, T 260.17 at rate 2.99; per-factor baselines as in section 6; S without E 329.91; T without S 260.17. Probes on scratch copies of the step world:
E — plan payment returned, not made good 12; returned and made good (restored tier) 13; plan payment returned on the other loan 14; a line on the other plan 14; a second line on 2026-09-15 (counted once) 14; rows reversed 14; the 2026-09-15 line missing with the end of service 2026-09-30 (lag due date covered) 14; end of service on the due day 2026-09-15 with that line missing (due date on the end day covered) 14; no plan installment line 0; no captured end of service 12; pre-plan installment 0 (no division) 12; 7% step (flat tier) 13; 365-day service with lag due dates covered 19.
S — end date empty 329.91; end date before the next due date 329.91; two to come (flat 50) 309.71; the later 2026-11-15 line after a credited 295.27 line 297.11; the 2026-09-15 line split into 194.35 + 100.00 (taken together as the previous line, in either row order) 295.27; an extra uncredited 100.00 line on 2026-09-15 (taken together, held to the pre-plan installment; the line record is spoilt) 334.76 in either row order; a covered next due date (end of service 2026-10-20, or on the due day 2026-10-15, or none captured) 294.35, the plan installment; a returned plan payment 330.72; the 800.00 returned 296.89; prepayment exactly twelve months before (outside) 296.89; prepayment on the other loan 296.89; AutoPay off 296.89; pre-plan below the previous line 294.35; plan and pre-plan installments 0 -> line 0.00, still scheduled; rows reversed 295.27.
T — one income statement (bank statement left) 262.81; income statement on the other plan only 262.81; 24 due dates left (level) 136.48; 48 left (interest only, raised to the 25.00 minimum) 25.00; maturity before next due (at least one due date) 260.17; AutoPay enrolled with no debit in the window 260.83; AutoPay return in the window 260.56; funded 24 months before 259.51; funded on the 31st, 11 whole months 260.83; loan rows reversed 260.17. Hold: at the opening the benefit is active with the end of service captured (applies) and has no line for 2026-10-15 (does not hold); after step 11 it has one.

10. SWEEP AND XF RECIPE (all 14 points re-applied in round 3). (1) Independence: factor bindings read only their own evidence and plain bindings (covered_due_dates, service_lines; plan_installment, prev_line, prev_amount, step_up, share_applied; loan_principal, due_dates_left, plan_rate; the repayment-shape factor owns scheduled_installment and current_rate_monthly, which only its principal-part tier uses); checked by script. (2) Assembly sentences are generic and order-fixed: "Every graduated-return due date that applies is added to the covered due dates; ..."; "Where another rule of this policy replaces the share of the step up charged, ... the share so reached is applied once to the step up and added to the previous line's amount"; "Where another rule of this policy replaces the program's plan_rate_percent or the level installment, ... the installment is worked once, at the rate so reached". (3) Factor-only quantities sit in their factor's own sentence: the due dates still to come are defined inside "Step schedule:", the payment step inside "Graduated return by payment step:", the plan record inside its ladder; covered due dates, the previous line and the step up are baseline quantities. (4) Overwrites as in section 5, each naming its own scope; the round-2 overwrite of the base start is withdrawn because the start now follows the base. (5) compute_basis quotes verbatim, superseded clauses verbatim in base (scratch sweep 0 misses). (6) Rounding: RND only on the final figure in S and T. (7) Docstrings: no example values, no ordering words, no other tool names. (8) Probes in section 9: decoys, absent records, None, zero division, ties (stated: several lines on one due date count once; the previous line's amount takes every line on that due date together, so row order never matters), month-end and the due-date-on-the-end-day boundary (stated: on or before the end of service is covered), look-back boundary, returned rows netted, 0.00 amounts. (9) Method shapes with distinguishing inputs: payment step {proportional >= 2 | flat 1 | none} by 12.07% / 7% / 3%; step schedule {100/(r+1) <= 25 | flat 50 | whole 100} by 6 / 2 / 0 due dates to come or an unpaid line; repayment {principal part + plan interest | interest only | level} by 12 / 48 / 24 due dates left. (10) No factor id is a substring of a tool name. (11) No cross-record date pairing. (12) Realism as in section 6; seeded rows are states the loan and hardship charters produce (start_date = service start, interest split at the service start, no retroactive credit owed). (13) frozen_time '2026-10-14 11:40:00 EDT'; tools import only erlbench and write in their own bodies. (14) Proof text swept after the round 3 changes.

11. SOLUTION AND CLOSURE. Reads: find_customers -> verify -> find_loans -> find_bank_accounts -> find_loan_transactions -> find_loan_servicing_events -> find_hardship_plans -> find_hardship_plan_events. Writes: unlock + hand over certification (P1, 2027-03-15, 14) -> schedule graduated-return line (P1, customer, L1, 2026-10-15, 295.27) -> offer rate reduction (P2, L2, 286.63, 12.99, 3175.56, 12, 2026-11-01, 2027-04-01, 2.99, 260.17). Policy -> tool -> step/arg -> terminal: service end -> report_military_service_end_1d04825e -> 8 plan_months -> P1.end_date/plan_months; graduated-return installment -> schedule_benefit_plan_installment_71e01653 -> 10 amount -> new line; rate reduction -> offer_rate_reduction_plan_52a2ad4e -> 12 plan_payment_amount -> P2 offered. Draft from the visible context: the rate-reduction hold applies on the opening records and sends the agent to the benefit, whose graduated-return rule waits on the certification; the published ladders on the read rows give 14 / 2027-03-15, 295.27 and 2.99% / 260.17 — equal to gold. Easily got wrong: offering the rate reduction first; recording the release date 2026-09-30 as the end date; counting the bank statement; using the level installment for a 12-due-date loan; scheduling the line before the certification (whole step up -> 329.91).

12. ROUND 4. The rate-reduction hold is scoped to a benefit with no end date recorded or an end date on or after the benefit loan's next due date: in a world where the benefit earns no graduated-return due date, the servicemember's certification records the last covered due date as end date, which falls before the next due date, so the hold no longer binds and the offer can be made in the same contact; in a world where lines lag the end of service, the line for a covered next due date is scheduled by the same graduated-return policy at the plan installment, so the declared problem governs it. On this world the hold applies at the opening (no end date) and still applies after the certification (2027-03-15 is after 2026-10-15), so the tree and every scored value are unchanged. Same-day previous lines are now taken together, independent of row order.

13. ROUND 5 (renderer source scan). The repayment-shape factor now owns the scheduled installment and the current monthly rate, the only quantities its principal-part tier reads, and its sentence states how due dates left are counted, as does the level-installment baseline; the graduated-return policy's shared twelve-month look-back sentence is gone, its AutoPay and prepayment sentences each carrying their own boundary; the certification tool now describes the end date for a benefit that covers no due date (the end of military service) and plan months 0. Gold and every sensitivity unchanged.

14. ROUND 6 (KB audit source items). The Servicemember overwrites no longer retire the unchanged "lower of" rate clause, and the covered-date installment has one description, the plan installment recorded on the benefit when it was applied (set then as the level payment at the capped rate), matching the compute. Gold and every sensitivity unchanged.

15. ROUND 7 (seed re-priced from the published loan rules). Every loan installment is now the level payment on the amount financed at the base rate over the term (Grade D 334.76, Grade C 286.63), unchanged when AutoPay starts; interest still accrues at the AutoPay-discounted rate (17.24, 12.99) on an actual/365 basis, so every interest and principal portion, both principal histories, the benefit's recorded unpaid principal (7159.76), its capped level payment (294.35 at 6.00 over 26 due dates), its eight lines, eight credits and eight plan payments, and both APRs were re-derived. The 2026-02-15 interest is again split at the 2026-01-20 service start (16.91 + 30.60 = 47.51), so no interest credit is owed. Each loan carries its AutoPay enrollment servicing record on its funding date (phone, the verified Synovus account), read by the new find_loan_servicing_events step. Gold moved with the seed: 14 / 2027-03-15 (unchanged), 295.27, 2.99% / 260.17; every factor still bears weight and both prerequisites are still unmet at the opening.
user_scenario:
You are Terrence J. Galloway, 36, from Columbus, Georgia. You are polite, brief and a little formal ("yes, sir" or "yes, ma'am" comes naturally to you), and you like the representative to tell you plainly what they are doing before they do it. You started a new job this month that pays noticeably less than your old one, and last Friday you asked online for a lower interest rate on your newer Larkspur loan, the auto-repair loan, and uploaded two pay statements and a bank statement with that request. You are calling because you want that rate-reduction request decided today and to hear what your lower payment would be. You are not asking to pay anything today, you are not asking for any fee to be waived, and you do not want to change your AutoPay.

To find your profile, give your mobile number, 7065552184. When the representative asks you to confirm your identity, give your date of birth as 1990-02-14 and your ZIP code as 31909; only if they say that is not enough do you add your email, terrence.galloway@gmail.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 2457. You do not remember balances or account numbers and you ask the representative to read them from the account.

Only if the representative asks about your military service or your other Larkspur loan do you explain that you are in the Army Reserve, that you received your mobilization orders on December 8, 2025 and sent them in with your benefit request that same day, that you reported for duty on January 20, 2026, that you have now been released from active duty with a release date of September 30, 2026, and that you uploaded your release orders on October 2. If the representative explains that you have to certify the end of your military service yourself and hands you that step, you do it on the spot, entering exactly the end date and the number of covered due dates the representative gives you, in the format they ask for, never values of your own. If the representative then tells you what your next payment on that other loan will be, you note it and say that is fine.

If the representative asks what your pay statements show, you read the figures off them: your gross monthly pay at your old job was 4,920.00 dollars and your gross monthly pay at your new job is 3,770.00 dollars. When the representative tells you the reduced interest rate and the monthly payment on your newer loan, you repeat them back once, say you will review the offer in the app before accepting it, thank them, and end the call.
